tower-of-hanoi.title: Goal Stack Ordering
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The goal configuration always requires the disks on the target peg to be ordered from the largest at the bottom to the smallest at the top. Recognizing this ordering tells you which disk must be placed directly on the goal peg first and the subsequent order of placements.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a Tower of Hanoi problem specifies a final arrangement, especially when all disks must end on a single peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: For 5 disks the goal stack on peg 2 must be [5,4,3,2,1] (bottom→top).

tower-of-hanoi.title: Place Larger Disks Before Smaller
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Because a larger disk may never sit on a smaller one, any disk that must appear below another on the goal peg has to be moved onto that peg first. Therefore the sequence of moves onto the goal peg is strictly decreasing in disk size.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the part of the solution that deposits disks onto the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Move disk 4 onto the goal peg before moving disk 3, then disk 2, then disk 1.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Free Blocked Disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: A disk that has smaller disks on top cannot be moved directly. The smaller disks must be relocated to other pegs (auxiliary or temporary) before the blocked disk can be moved.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever the desired disk to move is not the topmost on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move disk 4 from peg 0, first move disks 1 and 2 elsewhere.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use Auxiliary Peg for Temporary Storage
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The third peg (neither source nor target) serves as a temporary holding area for smaller disks while larger disks are being moved. Choose the auxiliary peg that does not contain a disk smaller than the one you intend to place there.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to clear a peg or store a sub‑tower temporarily.
tower-of-hanoi.example: While moving disk 4, store disks 1 and 2 on peg 1 (which currently holds disk 3).

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Sub‑tower Transfer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Moving a stack of k disks from one peg to another follows the classic recursion: move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, move the kth (largest) disk to the target, then move the k‑1 disks from auxiliary onto the target. This pattern works even when the initial configuration is split across pegs, as long as the relative ordering is respected.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to relocate a contiguous sub‑stack of several disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move disks 2 and 1 from peg 0 to peg 1, first move disk 1 to the free peg, then move disk 2, then move disk 1 onto disk 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Check Move Legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: A legal move must (a) take the topmost disk from the source peg, and (b) place it on a destination peg whose top disk is larger (or the peg is empty). Violating either condition makes the move illegal and the verifier will reject the sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before appending any move to the list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 3 onto a peg whose top is disk 2 is illegal because 3 > 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Simulate Final Configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After drafting the move list, mentally (or on paper) replay each move from the initial state to ensure the final arrangement matches the goal exactly. This catches missing or extra moves and illegal steps before submission.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you think you have a complete solution, before outputting it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Starting from the given stacks, apply each move in the list and verify the final stacks equal the goal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Maintain 0‑Indexed Peg Numbers
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The output format expects peg identifiers 0, 1, 2. Using 1‑based or other numbering will be parsed incorrectly and cause rejection.
tower-of-hanoi.example: The move “disk 1 from peg 0 to peg 2” is written as [1,0,2].

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid Premature Small‑Disk Placement on Goal
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Placing a small disk onto the goal peg before the larger disk that should sit beneath it blocks the larger disk, making the remaining moves impossible. Keep the goal peg free of any disk smaller than the next larger disk you intend to place there.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: While planning moves that involve the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Do not move disk 1 onto peg 2 before disk 4 has been placed there.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Track Current Top Disk on Each Peg
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Keeping an up‑to‑date mental list of the top disk on each peg lets you quickly decide which moves are legal and which disks are available. Update this list after every move.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Throughout the solving process, especially before deciding a move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After moving disk 1 from peg 0 to peg 2, the top of peg 0 becomes disk 2, and the top of peg 2 becomes disk 1.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Placing a larger disk onto a smaller one
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may forget the rule that a larger disk can never rest on a smaller disk, especially when focusing on freeing a blocked disk.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always compare the size of the moving disk with the top disk of the destination peg; the destination top must be larger or the peg must be empty.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model sometimes treats any disk on a peg as movable, ignoring that only the topmost disk may be moved.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before issuing a move, verify that the disk you intend to move is currently the topmost disk on its source peg.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Prematurely placing a small disk on the goal peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: In an effort to reduce the number of moves, the model may move a small disk onto the goal peg before the larger disk that should be beneath it, creating a dead‑end.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Follow the decreasing‑size order for placements onto the goal peg; never place a smaller disk there until all larger required disks are already positioned below it.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Confusion between human‑friendly 1‑based numbering and the required 0‑based indexing leads to wrong peg numbers in the output.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Remember that pegs are numbered 0, 1, 2 in the answer format; double‑check each move triple before finalizing.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Skipping final verification of the goal state
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may assume the constructed move list is correct without replaying it, leading to subtle errors that the verifier catches.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After writing the full move list, mentally simulate the entire sequence from the initial configuration to confirm the final stacks match the goal exactly.
